sources.text: Investigate and fix the 6 pre-existing 120-second test timeouts in apps/server adapter/runtime tests on nullStack65/t3code branch release/native-0.1.10, observed during the review of the standing-compaction pull request: 686 of 692 passed and 6 timed out at 120 seconds, including a native-fork test. Reproduce them, root-cause why they hang, and fix cleanly without weakening assertions. Verify the full affected suites pass fast and the server typecheck passes. Run exactly one independent review round on grok/grok-4.7, fixing any Critical, Important or Medium findings with a focused re-check. Open a pull request against release/native-0.1.10 with Deploy: none and full provenance. Do not merge.

requirements.title: Stop the apps/server adapter and runtime tests hanging or failing on stale approval and snooze behavior
acceptance_criteria: The full-access command approval auto-allows only when the session actually opened with bypass, so a workspace that downgrades the session still gets an approval request instead of a caller waiting until the test timeout.
A removal check and a permission-rule denial still fail closed in every mode a full-access thread can open.
The usage-limit tests arm recovery the way the code does now, through auto-resume, and apply a snooze only as the per-thread snooze, and the projection test checks the candidate query directly.
The affected suites pass without a 120-second timeout and the server typecheck reports no errors.

coverage.note: The task arrived as an agent handoff with no user-authored source, so this stays a proposal and lists no files or checks. The work is done and checked: ClaudeAdapterV2.test.ts passed 460, the usage-limit and projection cases passed 24, the three affected files together passed 700 with one pre-existing ordering failure at runtimeLayer.test.ts:2297, and the server typecheck reported no errors. The changed files are listed under unrequested until a user accepts the proposal.

non_goals: Fixing the pre-existing wake-ordering flake at runtimeLayer.test.ts:2297, which fails independently of this change.
Merging the pull request or changing deployment.
Changing the usage-limit recovery behavior itself; only the tests that assumed the removed snooze arming were updated.
